clue.text: Seating accommodation for members

parts.note: members here are limbs, so the accommodation is the space a seated passenger has for their legs

explanation.surface: Seats set aside for the members of a club or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The space in front of a seat in a plane or car is measured by how much the passenger's legs can stretch.

clue.text: Lap speed

definitions.meaning: to lap is to ... up liquid with the tongue
a ... is a fast pace, as in going at a fair ...

explanation.surface: A runner measures the speed of each lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat laps milk with its tongue, and at a great rate is an informal phrase for great speed.

clue.text: Crew said to assess means to get on ship

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers

indicators.note: said signals that the next word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to weigh something up is to assess it

explanation.surface: Sailors are said to judge how to board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIGH sounds like WAY, which is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is the movable bridge by which people board or leave a vessel.

clue.text: Sketch of ball on green in Open

parts.note: a round ball drawn as a picture looks like the letter O
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A drawing of a golf ball on the green at the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's championship; here it means unconcealed. Vert is green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done publicly, not hidden.

clue.text: Nearly overlook main source of trouble

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to miss something is to overlook it
chief means main or principal

explanation.surface: Almost ignoring the main cause of a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful or harmful behaviour that causes annoyance or damage.

clue.text: Immobilise car first, having no front light

indicators.note: first says the car is put before the word for immobilise
having no front tells us the opening letter of the combined run is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to immobilise a parked car is to clamp it, fitting a wheel lock

explanation.surface: A wheel-clamping warden immobilises a car whose headlight is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the car ahead of the clamp; 'having no front' then drops the opening C of that combined run. 'light' at the end is the definition, not part of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is an electric light in which a spark jumps between two electrodes.

clue.text: As worker nursing disease might be?

definitions.text: As worker nursing disease might be?

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: An employee looking after an illness might well be off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' holds the pieces inside; read as a whole, the clue also describes a sick employee staying off work, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off work through illness is not present at their job.

clue.text: Section of richer bourgeoisie in French town

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the wealthier middle class lives in a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherbourg is a port town in Normandy, France.

clue.text: Such entertaining nights, following MI?

parts.note: MI in Roman numerals is a thousand and one, the number of nights in the famous tale collection

explanation.surface: Nights out are fun after a spell in military intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: MI looks like Military Intelligence, but read as Roman numerals it is 1001, as in The Thousand and One Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The collection of tales told by Scheherazade is known as the Arabian Nights' Entertainments.

clue.text: Scout, of course, made new friend

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: made new says the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A Scout naturally makes a new friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathfinder is someone who goes ahead to find the route, a scout.

clue.text: Trick meaning almost out of order, in the majority view

parts.note: to con is to trick or swindle

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sense is a synonym of meaning
U/S, short for unserviceable, means broken or out of order

explanation.surface: A con trick that is barely working is judged by most people to be out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SENSE to SENS; US is a British abbreviation for unserviceable, used of broken equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is the general agreement reached by most people in a group.

clue.text: Record performance, showing difference between years

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A record-breaking performance shows how much one year differs from another.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the number of days by which the solar year exceeds the lunar year.

clue.text: Crew fight ban I contrived, following instructions to lawyer

indicators.note: contrived means put together artificially, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crew's fight leads to a ban, and a lawyer is told to follow events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges the thirteen letters of CREW FIGHT BAN I.
explanation.definitionFit: A watching brief is a barrister's instruction to observe a case on behalf of an interested party not directly involved.

clue.text: Maybe he goes into capitals as an overseas rep

definitions.text: Maybe he goes into capitals as an overseas rep

parts.words: Maybe he goes into capitals as an overseas rep
parts.note: a diplomat representing his country is posted to foreign capital cities

explanation.surface: A rep travels to major cities abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitals hints at capital letters, but it means capital cities where embassies stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior diplomat heads his country's embassy in a foreign capital.

clue.text: Is Tom's mate allowed a choice of girls for celebration?

definitions.text: a choice of girls for celebration

parts.note: may expresses permission, so allowed gives may
a tom is a male cat and a female cat is called a queen

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Tom's partner may pick from several girls for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name, but it is a tomcat, whose mate is a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Each May Day a village girl is chosen and crowned to preside over the festivities.

clue.text: Deviating from annual revelling, if routine's held up

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece goes within the other
revelling suggests riotous disorder, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled
up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: Wild yearly partying is abnormal if normal life stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revelling' scrambles the annual letters into UNNAAL, and 'up' turns the routine word into TUR, which 'held' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural means departing from what is normal or expected.

clue.text: Attack a provocative performance

definitions.meaning: to round on someone suddenly and assault them
something that arouses or excites, such as a sexy show

explanation.surface: A provocative show on stage is attacked by the critics.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to set upon someone, and the noun means anything that excites desire.

clue.text: Making sure one's watch keeps going

definitions.text: Making sure one's watch keeps going

parts.words: Making sure one's watch keeps going
parts.note: watch is a guard duty rather than a timepiece, and one keeps it by staying alert

explanation.surface: Someone checks that their wristwatch does not stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch looks like a timepiece needing winding; it is a period of guard duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry who stays alert throughout his duty is watchful.

clue.text: Abused plain English at European summits

indicators.note: abused means treated badly or mangled, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plain English is mistreated at meetings of European leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abused' reworks PLAIN into ALPIN. Summits looks like political meetings, but it means mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes the high mountains of Europe, so it means found on their peaks.

clue.text: Stick out long-term study

definitions.meaning: a planned piece of research carried out over time

explanation.surface: Someone persists with a lengthy piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to protrude; as a noun it is a planned undertaking or piece of research.

clue.text: More of a drag?

parts.note: a drag is a puff on a cigarette, and a longer cigarette gives more of them

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is more tedious than ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra-long cigarettes are sold under a label meaning larger than standard.

clue.text: Works in pubs — a way to be accepted

indicators.note: to be accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone works in pubs as a way of fitting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb about bar jobs; it is a noun for a machine's insides. RD is the usual abbreviation for road.
explanation.definitionFit: The works of a machine are its internal parts, its insides.

clue.text: Money blackguard raised for pompous dictator

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain raises funds for an arrogant tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-important person who behaves as if beyond criticism is mocked as a petty idol.

clue.text: Calculation of numbers in light infantry, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a method of dividing numbers done mentally without writing out the working
taken literally, a small army unit, since light troops might be thought of as a little division

explanation.surface: Counting the soldiers in a light infantry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic method divides by a small number without long written steps; an army division is a large military unit.

clue.text: Film company, perhaps, using latest device for cutting

parts.note: in means fashionable, the latest thing
a die is a tool for stamping or cutting shapes

explanation.surface: A film company uses the newest cutting equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent film or record company is called by this short informal name.

clue.text: To tax the population, taking final contributions? Neat

indicators.note: final contributions means the last letter of each of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A tidy way to tax everyone is to collect their last payments.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, so its plural is these beasts.

clue.text: Gloomy reading, for example, in letter's introduction

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a letter traditionally opens with Dear
reading is one of the three Rs, so it gives R

explanation.surface: A depressing book has to be read in the opening of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, each represented by R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal or bleak.

clue.text: Pole's at the front in this race, initially

definitions.text: Pole's at the front in this race, initially

parts.words: Pole's at the front in this race, initially
parts.note: pole position is the starting spot at the front of the grid in motor racing, so the leader begins there

explanation.surface: A Polish runner leads a race from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person; it is pole position, the front of the starting grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Formula One championship race starts with the fastest qualifier in pole position.

clue.text: Went quickly, being nervous

definitions.meaning: to rattle along is to move fast with a clatter
a person who is shaken or flustered

explanation.surface: Someone hurried away because they were frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to clatter along at speed, and the adjective means unsettled or agitated.

clue.text: Court finally given motive for serious crime

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word before it is taken

parts.note: a reason is a motive for doing something

explanation.surface: A court is at last told why the accused committed a grave offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest offence against the state.
